chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Father's death and building a house in Maine, 1945-47
summary: After his father died in 1945 he went home to Maine, designed and built a house with insurance money, and then John Kirby called him back to the Aquarium in 1947.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I had gone back home then, I went back because my father died-- that was 1945, just before the D-Day.
Uh huh. And you played with Dorsey until '45 -- that's when you left.
And I went back home; I had a little piece of land that my father had left there, that my aunt gave me.
But I never figured that -- I had a little insurance money that I put together with the land that I got -- we had a 35-acre farm. And my aunt gave me a piece

of property there, an acre and a half or two acres, and I built a house; I thought maybe that would do it. And I designed the house, I did the architecture myself, I got the money from the insurance, the local musicians -- contractors, and designed it, I got some stone masons there, they were 80 and 82 years old -- and built a lovely home, but I didn't figure that I needed money to make a living. I had the home, and no money.
And, John Kirby called me to come back and go to the Aquarium. So the house was just finished, it wasn't even painted inside, and I came back, and that must have been in '47.
